resources.string:
Say hello to the new Sky Map

Sky Map has been completely rebuilt from scratch — a new rendering engine, a new astronomy engine, and a new interface, made to be faster, more accurate, and easier on the eyes. Versions 2.1 and 2.2 build on that with some of the most-requested features:

Sky alerts

Sky Map can now tell you when something is worth stepping outside for: Meteor shower peaks and a Tonight\'s sky digest. Choose which alerts you want under Settings → Notifications, or from the Meteor showers layer.

Layer help

Not sure what a layer shows? Long-press any layer in the layers menu, or on the left-hand side of the map, to see what it does and what you can customise. The right ascension and declination grid can also be customised, like the alt/az grid.

Sky Map on your home screen

Three new widgets put the sky in your launcher: Moon phase (the phase, how much is lit, and moonrise and moonset, plus the Moon\'s age), Tonight\'s sky (sunset, when it gets dark, and the best sights tonight) and Sky countdown (days until the next meteor shower peak or moon event). Add one from the new Widgets menu item, or from your launcher\'s widget picker.

Also new in version 2

  • Steadier view: the picture shakes less and keeps up better when you move. Turn it off under Settings → Sensors → Smooth sensor movement if you prefer the raw sensor.
  • Searchable Help: results jump straight to the relevant part of the app.
  • Alt/az grid: overlay altitude and azimuth lines alongside the celestial grid. It\'s off by default — turn it on from the layers menu.
  • A fresh look: the new Deep Space / Star Gold colour scheme and sharper Sun, Moon and planet artwork.
  • More accurate Sun and Moon: the Moon sits where you see it, and eclipses and conjunctions land at the right minute.
  • A more realistic solar system: the Moon\'s phase is calculated from its true geometry, Venus, Mercury and Mars show phases, and you can view planets at their real size.
  • Lunar eclipses: the Moon turns its copper-red tint on the map.
  • Find more stars: 268 new IAU star names, and search by Bayer or Flamsteed designation — "α Cyg" finds Deneb.
  • Live readout: right ascension and declination, altitude and azimuth, and field of view, right on the map.
  • 28 languages, fully translated.

And this is just the start...

We have many long asked-for features coming very soon.
